entities.summary: Art Nouveau was an influential international philosophy and style of art, architecture, and applied art that originated around 1890 CE. This movement, characterized by sinuous lines, organic forms, and a focus on functionality, emerged in Europe and spread globally, influencing various artistic fields. Notable figures associated with Art Nouveau include Alphonse Mucha, Gustav Klimt, and Louis Comfort Tiffany. The style's popularity peaked during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with its heyday in Paris and Vienna. Art Nouveau's impact can be seen in the works of artists such as Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Edward Burne-Jones, and John William Waterhouse. The movement's legacy continues to inspire contemporary artists and designers. As "The International Style," Art Nouveau played a significant role in the development of modern art and architecture. The style's emphasis on harmony and balance influenced the work of architects like Antoni Gaudí and Victor Horta. Art Nouveau's influence can also be seen in the decorative arts, with the style's characteristic motifs and patterns appearing in jewelry, textiles, and ceramics. The movement's focus on functionality and the integration of art and design into everyday life also anticipated modern design principles. Art Nouveau's significance can be measured by its impact on modern art and architecture, as well as its continued influence on contemporary design.
